findings.title: Keep the invocation deadline effective through terminal publication
findings.body: Both producers cancel ITIMER_REAL and snapshot elapsed_seconds before serializing and fsyncing the terminal, rotated summary and terminal event; neither rechecks remaining_seconds afterward. If final publication straddles the admitted deadline, especially on an explicitly reduced-time resume, this path can finish with status complete and exit_code 0 despite exceeding that invocation allowance. The retained service copies enforce their full 300/180-second ceilings, not every smaller grant accepted by admit. The current successful runs are not shown to have exceeded their grants; the defect is the new finalization path and its advertised BOOT-through-exit accounting.

findings.consumer_impact: A Root consumer relying on the immutable successful terminal and its remaining-time accounting can accept an over-allowance finalization. Existing executed consumers require complete/exit0 but do not independently enforce a smaller invocation deadline.
findings.narrow_correction: Keep publication inside the admitted time authority: retain deadline enforcement through final writes and make an over-deadline finalization fail, with bounded failure-receipt handling. Ensure the enclosing manager deadline is derived from the exact invocation grant, including reduced resumes. Label the in-process timestamp as a pre-publication snapshot and use the existing post-exit owner receipt for through-exit accounting rather than claiming that a receipt can measure its own later fsync/exit.

findings.title: Stop full metadata writes when the output allowance is exhausted
findings.body: OutputRun.finish detects insufficient output allowance but merely changes status and then still writes the full terminal and summary; the factor finalizer performs the same full writes with no cap check. A grant too small to fund metadata, or a resumed output directory already at its granted limit, therefore continues adding files after the budget failure. admit currently accepts any positive output_max_bytes up to the ceiling, so the fixed reserve does not eliminate this path: configure/budget can reject the run and then finally performs the writes anyway. This violates the output cap precisely on its failure path.

evidence.detail: The check rejects exhausted allowance, but finish unconditionally writes full terminal/summary/event after its own cap branch.
A configure/check failure still flows through run.finish.
Budget checks reserve metadata during production, but final terminal/summary/event writes do not enforce the remaining output allowance.
Only a positive upper-bounded integer is required; no minimum metadata reservation is admitted.
Factor context publication also precedes grant admission.

findings.consumer_impact: A failed or resumed bounded producer can exceed Root-owned disk-output authority while reporting an output-cap failure. The manager memory/time limits do not enforce aggregate output bytes.
findings.narrow_correction: Admit enough output authority for the actual context and bounded failure receipt before full publication. On an exhausted-output branch, preserve existing immutable artifacts and publish only a compact receipt that fits a genuinely reserved allowance; do not unconditionally duplicate full source/output inventories into terminal and summary files. Apply the same finalization rule to both producers.
findings.verification_status: Static control-flow finding only; no cap-failure execution was authorized or performed. No output-cap breach is claimed for the supplied successful runs.
findings.current_artifact_effect: The existing complete outputs and exact-readback evidence remain usable; this is a correction to failure/reuse boundaries, not to numerical arrays.
